speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, please take a seat. I understand you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, as well as episodes of pain during urination, and a history of a similar swollen ankle that resolved on its own. To better understand what is happening, have you noticed any redness or warmth over the affected joints?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, sexual history, and the pattern of migratory joint involvement (ankle then knee) alongside urinary symptoms, I suspect a reactive arthritis or gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and Gram stain of urine. REQUEST TEST: Synovial fluid analysis from the right knee. REQUEST TEST: Gonorrhea and Chlamydia NAAT.

text: The urinalysis confirms sterile pyuria with white blood cells, while the synovial fluid shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis without bacteria on Gram stain. Given your recent sexually active history and migratory arthritis, we need to rule out a urethral infection that triggered a reactive process. REQUEST TEST: Urine NAAT for Gonorrhea and Chlamydia. Do you currently have any discharge from your penis or testicular pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: The synovial fluid analysis reveals a high white blood cell count with neutrophil predominance, indicating an inflammatory process, but the absence of bacteria on Gram stain makes septic arthritis less likely. While your recent sexual history raises concern for gonococcal infection, the lack of discharge and negative initial NAAT pushes me toward reactive arthritis. Did you notice any eye redness, sore throat, or skin rashes like psoriasis or pustules recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's Syndrome), likely triggered by a prior Chlamydia infection.
